steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Are you really going to Kajimachi, Mifune-san?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: This is between me, Tessai, and Hoshiguma. I have to put an end to it personally.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: If things go according to your plan, Tessai will yield, even without Hannya.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Does the idea of Hoshiguma coming back upset you so?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: I don't see the need for it.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: True, you would have much more work to do if she came back. I'll tell you this plainly, since you'll someday take over for me.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: What do you think is the most important to living well in Mitsukue?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Unity?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: No... the most important thing is beauty.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: A fine appearance will turn the people's prejudices on their head. You and I, we all benefit from it.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: If I kept looking like a thug, they would've kicked me off camera the first time I was on TV. I never could have built Kinseki Channel into what it is today.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: It's important that we conduct our business with the proper look, with beauty.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: There is an Ursine author—his name escapes me—he says that if a gun appears in the first act of a story...

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Then a Lateran must hold it by the third act, at the latest.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: I believe there is a Columbian group by the name of Blacksteel that uses guns as well, Mifune-san.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Well, you know what I mean.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Mitsukue is too big, and it has grown too quickly. A lot of times, it's hard for us to tell if we're doing the right thing...

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: And so, we must make sure that everything we do has a proper beginning and end, that everyone is in their proper place, and the trigger of every gun is pulled by the end. This is the proper appearance. This is beauty.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: If I get your meaning... you want to see everything through to the bitter end.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Think of it however you want. Feel free to put my words to the test, once you become the Fourth Chairman of the Kinsekikai.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Right now, though, you should prepare to deal with Hoshiguma.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: She is a tough one.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: But she is an Oni, and one who has already gone berserk once.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Have you heard of an individual by the name of Qui'lon?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: All I know is that he lived a very long time ago, and had something to do with the Oni and the temples.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Setting aside those old warrior stories, it's this legend that Tessai talked about the most.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: I don't know if they are true, and they're often contradictory. For example, Tessai has told at least three different versions of how Qui'lon died.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: But my favorite version is cruel... and beautiful.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Before he reached nirvana and entered Kaśjñāna, Qui'lon heard the cries of the last Oni when they were forced to become people of Ashihara.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: By then, however, Qui'lon no longer had the strength to leave Ashoka, nor wield a sword to save his people, or even keep his fiery blue wrath in check—

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: The flames of rage took over Qui'lon's soul. He lost all reason, and in his mad rampage destroyed an entire army even as he lay at the gates of death, but the kin whom he was trying to protect were also destroyed by his sword.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: It is unknown whether Qui'lon died of exhaustion, or took his own life, or whether he was so heartless that he attained nirvana, fully at peace with himself, in spite of what he did.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: I'm not sure why you're telling me the legend of Qui'lon right now.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: An Oni is at its frailest when it realizes its own powerlessness. As to whether what follows next is depression or madness...

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Our foe has already demonstrated the answer, once.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Now, get some rest. I have a guest to greet.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Mifune-san... I bid you good health.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You're not hurt, are you?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: No, no! I haven't slept better in a long while!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Yes, in your line of work, it's important to be of good humor, to smile...

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: To be inquisitive.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Call Hoshiguma. Tell her that... I have something to discuss.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: See, Mifune-san... Hoshiguma helped me a lot, you know...

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Helped you discover the truth of the Wanyuudou?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Yes—

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: But not only that, right?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: What was going through your mind when you stood in front of your yatai, at a loss? Thinking about all those years you wasted chasing the kaidan, weren't you?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Now you know it was all fabricated. You were fooled by me and these kaidan stories I made up.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Why... Why did you do it?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: None of your business. Just think of it as a stroke of bad luck. But life goes on, after all. So, if you're willing, there's something more concrete you can seize.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Are you trying to bribe me?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Bribe? No. Make the call, and you can keep up your little information broker gig going. Refuse, and you know what the Kinsekikai does to our enemies.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Mifune-san—

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Would you like a reminder of how you lost your right eye?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: I haven't forgotten. I barged in on one of your negotiations while chasing a kaidan...

spans.text: I haven't forgotten. I barged in on one of your

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: I took one eye because you saw what you shouldn't have seen. I let you keep the other because I valued your talent, and as a warning to you.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Now, it's time you showed some gratitude.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Please, give me a few minutes to think—
Mifune slowly draws his blade.
Moriuchi's gaze is fixed upon the blade's tip, as it slowly moves to his own throat.
He gulps, unsure whether to open his mouth or close it—

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: What's that sound?
The office door is kicked open before Moriuchi can even react.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: H-Hoshiguma?!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Go!

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: But you...

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: He can't keep me. And I have questions for him.
Moriuchi takes one long look at Hoshiguma and hastily leaves.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: You don't seem anxious that I took someone from right under your nose.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Why should I be anxious, when something that I thought would take so much effort suddenly sorted itself out on its own?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Why did you forge that letter to bring me back?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: It's complicated. I just told the story to somebody else, and I'm not in the mood to tell it again.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: But the Old Man must know the simplest reason, however slow he might be... Hannya.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hannya?!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You didn't even think of that? Some yakuza! No wonder he made an enemy out of his own son, him and his beloved Ao-Oni of Kinsekikai!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Mio!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: I'm afraid your break's over. Stall her.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: You think your boys can beat Uncle Tessai if you stall me? Keep dreaming.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Why do you think victory is just a question of combat?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: What are you planning, then?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You'll see.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Now, I'd better be going.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hold it right there—

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You'll be the one holding it, actually.
Fire, and humming.
The scattered screens continue to stand, unmoving.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: They've escorted Mifune-san away. I will be your opponent.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Your blade. Draw it.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: No need for the blade if it's you.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Is that so?
With the unpleasant sound of metal against metal, a black ethereal hand appears from behind Mio, leisurely wrapping itself around a white tantou.
Three hands, three blades.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You're strong, but that doesn't mean you have what it takes to get away from me, much less without drawing your blade.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: You think the sword's my only weapon?
Before she finishes her sentence, Hoshiguma raises her right leg high and brings it down on the round table beside her, with great force.
The table flies into the air, blocking her opponent's view.
With a powerful leap, Hoshiguma points her sheathed sword at her foe's head—
Three flashes greet her, cutting the table open like a hot knife through butter.
The sheath encounters the black hand, delivering great force—

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hyaaah!

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: ...Impressive power.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Why don't you draw your blade?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: None of your business.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You're afraid.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Afraid? Me?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You're afraid that drawing your blade will cause something that you don't want to happen.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Qui'lon's death... I see.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: But what you fear will happen, whether you draw your blade or not, it will be your inevitable end. Assuming Mifune-san's predictions are accurate.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I don't really get it.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Despicable.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: No, not you.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Me.
Run. Flee.
Moriuchi does not know how long he has been running. He can feel his own innards shaking and trembling.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Huff... huff... huff...

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: D-Did I shake them?
You got out on your own?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: Forgot me so soon?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: K-Kami-sama?

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm not here to help you. I don't like the answer about the kaidan that I got at your yatai.

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: I kind of hate it.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: I... I get that.

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: I had planned on cutting ties with you and the kaidan entirely, perhaps even leave Mitsukue and take a trip to the north.

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: But someone asked me to do something.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: The kannushi? He asked you to find me?

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: Not him.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Who else could it be, then?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: You don't mean—

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: It asked me to bring you a single message.

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: 'Meet me on your usual rooftop.'

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: C-Could it be...?

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: I've delivered the message. It's time to go.
The kami turns around on its unicycle. No sooner has it got on than it sees Moriuchi is already a long way off.

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: ...Is this how you repay him, when he's searched for you for so many years?

steps.name: Nosy Kami
steps.text: You know what, it's none of my business.
Moriuchi runs up the steps.
He is running as hard as he can.
A breeze blows in Moriuchi's face as he opens the door.
Many a sunset has he watched lying on this rooftop, watching the sky turn from red to black, until the stars appear, before their light is overcome by the neon city.
The hour is early, and the sky should not look like dusk, but he pays little heed. Perhaps he considers it a sign of the coming of a kami.
He could not describe his own emotions as he gazes at the sky.
Excitement? Anxiety? Fulfillment? Emptiness? Sadness?
But he lies there, waiting for a guest who may never come...
Until the warm breeze sends him into slumber.

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Father... I think there's something behind the Kamidana.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Behave yourself, Tooru! This is a sacred shrine!

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: But it's really there...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Come, Tooru, it's our turn to pray.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Please, Kami-sama, keep our family safe, and may we repay our debts soon...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: There... the debt should be settled, with some money left over even...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: We're out of the woods!

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Wh-What are you doing here? Are you bored of the shrine?

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Kami-sama, arigatou!

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Father's mood has gotten a lot better, and mother has had time to take me out.

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Can I come and see you again?

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: —No, I'll definitely come and see you again!

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: Our shop just opened! It's really pretty. Do you want to come and see it?

steps.name: Young Moriuchi
steps.text: I'm sorry, Kami-sama, I've been busy helping out at home and haven't had time to come see you... please, don't be angry and let me see you?

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: K-Kami-sama? Are you still there? Did you leave? Or... do you not want to see me anymore?

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: I-I'll treat it like you don't want to see me, but you're still listening to me, okay?

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: Some things have happened at home. Father may have to go back to manual labor.

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: Mother's been sewing clothes for other people. Her eyesight's declining.

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: But I'm sure none of that has anything to do with you. You gave so many blessings to our family. Surely you wouldn't take it all back...

steps.name: Adolescent Moriuchi
steps.text: Surely...

steps.name: Adult Moriuchi
steps.text: Kami-sama, Father...

steps.name: Adult Moriuchi
steps.text: Father is dead. Overdrinking. The blow was too great for him.

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: ...Where are you?

steps.name: Moriuchi
steps.text: Please, Kami-sama... where are you?

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: This haunted house...

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: It's empty... something's not right!

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: It's connected to the nomadic city's superstructure?

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: H-How am I suppose to search this place? This is far more than just one house or Kajimachi. The whole plate might be connected...

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: No, don't get discouraged. As long as I find that bastard—

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Wh-What's this?!
Tetsuya stands dumbfounded, staring at dozens of crates that someone has stacked up here.
He blinks a few times and opens one of them.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: It's... weapons?!

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Katana, crossbows... grenade launchers...

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Is that... the Hoashi emblem? That major Northern Court clan? Is this where they hid their weapons?
He takes down a weapon-filled crate and opens the one underneath it, finding Northern Court standard-issue provisions and medical supplies inside.
He furiously takes the crates down one by one, opening all of them.
All contain military supplies manufactured by the Northern Court, every single one.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Th-The Northern Court weapons that Papa says aren't here? But they are—

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: You've gone too far, boy.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: Oyabun wanted you to look for traces of Northern Court spies. It's enough that you found them. You've made a lot of work opening these up, one-by-one.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: ...Did you just take my picture?

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: This is big, after all. Best keep some evidence, to prevent disputes.

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: To see Mifune-san.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: W-Wait, you were stalking me?

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: That's not important. What's important is that you're working for Mifune-san, and so am I.

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: And take that mask off.

steps.name: Tetsuya
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Hidden Ninja
steps.text: You're meeting the oyabun. It's a little disrespectful to have your mask on, isn't it?
For some reason, Tetsuya feels a chill run up his spine, perhaps from the cold wind blowing in from the tunnels, but he has no choice but to comply.
